answer: Payouts hinge on a bilateral receipt graph. Each job needs a counterparty's countersignature, and an identity is credited only when its receipts come from three partners on different ridges of that graph, with no shared funding or key ancestry. The registry merges same-ridge clusters, so a thousand puppets collapse into one knoll and split one slot's reward. Escrow stays locked while a merge is contested; contesting costs an onyx bond, forfeited if the edges prove incestuous. Sybils must then trade genuinely with outside agents at market rates each epoch, far costlier than throwaway keys.
